summary: @servicetitan/forge preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a React UI component library but its preinstall lifecycle hook (`node setup.mjs`) downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases, marks it executable, and invokes it against a bundled 727 KB file `math_init.js` that is not referenced by the library's public API in forge.cjs. `math_init.js` begins with a `// @bun @bun-cjs` header and is heavily obfuscated in the obfuscator.io style (rotated string array via a `WV8StW` shift rotator, hex-mangled `_0x` identifiers, hundreds of encoded constants), making its runtime behavior opaque. The loader itself, setup.mjs, is also obfuscated with hex-mangled identifiers and per-function wrapper-property maps (e.g. `_0x19328d.YCZJE(execFileSync, 'ldd',...)`) that indirect ordinary calls — a shape inconsistent with a normal native-dependency installer. Executing the payload via a freshly dropped Bun binary bypasses Node-based inspection tooling and runs attacker-controlled logic on every installer's machine at `npm install` time, regardless of whether the consumer intends to use the library. The combination of alternate-runtime dropper, purpose mismatch with the package's stated function, obfuscated loader, and obfuscated payload matches the install-time remote-code-execution attack pattern.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
